findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple live nymphs along the wall of the back storage room, between the soda boxes and standing coolers. Multiple dead and live roaches (in various sages of development) were observed on glue traps today. A dead roach was also observed directly beneath the soda lid holders (in an area the inspector noted was in need of cleaning during the last inspection).
Glue traps have either NOT been date marked, or not REPLACED since the last follow up inspection. Today is the third follow up inspection since 09/15 original inspection, and the proliferation of roaches has gotten worse. 
Roach sightings are being logged in a blue Steritech binder, however only two sightings have been noted since the last follow up. The facility has increased the frequency at which pest control services the establishment to biweekly, however the presence of nymphs indicates that the adults are breeding.
Facility must coordinate cleaning efforts with maintenance (to fill and seal holes/ gaps which may be harboring roaches), as well as their pest control operator to ensure the elimination and of harborage conditions, and to stop the proliferation of roaches.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed some of the under counter cabinets at the concession stand to contain large holes between the cabinets, which may be prime conditions for pest harborage. Coordinate with maintenance to ensure these holes are filled. All nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable. Inspector will check that these physical facilities have been sealed on 12/17.
findings.citation_text: 4-402.11(A) Fixed Equipment, Spacing or Sealing. (A) EQUIPMENT that is fixed because it is not EASILY MOVABLE shall be installed so that it is: (1) Spaced to allow access for cleaning along the sides, behind, and above the EQUIPMENT; (2) Spaced from adjoining EQUIPMENT, walls, and ceilings a distance of not more than 1 millimeter or one thirty-second inch; or (3) SEALED to adjoining EQUIPMENT or walls, if the EQUIPMENT is exposed to spillage or seepage. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed food debris throughout the facility, including significant films of grease in some under counter cabinets. There is signifcant soiling of the cabinets directly underneath the soda lid holders on the back side of the service counter. 
Food contact and nonfood contact surfaces should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris. The facility requires increased managerial oversight to ensure conditions for pest harborage (see violation #38) are eliminated. Managers that open the facility must communicate with managers that close the facility, and coordinate cleaning schedules. Establish cleaning schedules and encourage cleaning during lapses between customers. Inspector will return on 12/08/25 to check cleaning.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Multiple physical facilities are observed to contain a significant accumulation of food and other soil debris:
1) The floor and drainage pipe next to the soda boxes contain liquid pooling, and a significant amount of soil accumulation.
2) The floor and wall on the East wall behind the soda boxes in the food storage room.
3) Behind the water heater.
 Ensure floors and walls are cleaned at a frequency to prevent soil accumulation. Inspector will return on 12/08 to checking cleaning.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed one dead roach in a cabinet. CORRECTED. Education was provided to the person in charge (PIC) regarding reduction of pest harborage. The area was cleaned up, with the roach removed. Continue cleaning areas where food debris or grease may be harbored. Reduce moisture and check dark spaces for harborage conditions, as roaches are nocturnal pests.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple dead roaches on insect traps, as well as in the under-counter cabinetry. Live roaches were also observed on the traps, from adult to larval stages. Employees are currently logging pest sightings in a blue “Steritech” binder. Nine roach sightings have been reported during the past month in the binder in areas including the bar, near the water heater, in the manager office, as well as in areas where ready-to-eat food is held. On 10/07/25 the pest control technician noted that the areas in the pest log had been chemically treated, and gel bait was applied.

 If dead roaches are spotted they should be immediately removed, and the area they were in should be cleaned. Remove all conditions for harborage, including spilt food and beverages, as well as cardboard. Write the date on glue traps to better monitor pests. The frequency at which pest control is providing services to the facility is currently inadequate. Increase services to biweekly treatments. The inspector will return on 10/29/25 to check pest control management. Ensure the facility has proof of service available as well as a minimum six month contract with a pest control provider to show during the follow up inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed food contact sanitizer bottle reading 0 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- the sanitizer bottle was remade to have a concentration of 200 ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizer is made (and tested using the facility’s test strips) at a frequency to hold the proper concentration as recommended by the manufacturer’s label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed soil accumulation on the soda nozzles at the bar, as well as inside the nozzle holder. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) moved the nozzles to be cleaned and sanitized, and wiped the nozzle holder with a clean sanitizing cloth. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil debris.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Nacho cheese containers on the south hold holding unit were observed to have ambient temperatures ranging from 115-120. The PIC stated the cheeses had been there at least since yesterday. CORRECTED- PIC voluntarily discarded 28 containers of nacho cheese, and a probe thermometer was placed in the hot holding unit to monitor ambient temperatures. Ensure all hold holding units allow internal temperatures of temperature control for safety (TCS) foods to reach 135F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

1) The hinges around the artisan popcorn contain an accumulation of dust and food debris.
2) The gaskets of the hotdog under counter cooler contain an accumulation of mold.
3) Soil accumulation behind the un-adhered board underneath the pick up station. 
4) Counter above the lid drawers (behind northern most register). 
5) Underneath the lid pop out storage directly to the left of the northernmost register.
Nonfood contact surfaces should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris to prevent contamination of food.
